# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wong_2026_ginisortamab"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wong_2026_ginisortamab"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70567> (open access; the Supporting
  Information holds the NONMEM control stream of the final model, Tables S1-S3
  and Figures S1-S3)

Ginisortamab is a human IgG monoclonal antibody that binds gremlin-1, a bone
morphogenetic protein (BMP) antagonist, and restores BMP signalling. The model
describes serum free ginisortamab and serum total gremlin-1 with a
two-compartment, quasi-steady-state target-mediated drug disposition
(TMDD-QSS) model, and is used to predict suppression of free gremlin-1.

# Population

The model was fitted to 25 adults with recurrent or metastatic advanced solid
tumours associated with GREM1 mRNA expression in the monotherapy
dose-escalation module of the first-in-human ONC001 study (NCT04393298, UK
sites). Participants received ginisortamab 100, 250, 500, 1000 or 2000 mg as a
60-min intravenous infusion every 2 weeks (Q2W). Median age was 64 years
(range 37-74), 32% were female, median weight 69 kg (46-116), median BMI
24 kg/m^2 (19-36) and median body surface area (BSA) 1.8 m^2 (1.4-2.4); 92%
were White. The most common tumours were colorectal (11/25), pancreatic (6/25)
and prostate (3/25) adenocarcinoma. All participants were anti-drug-antibody
negative. The analysis used 371 ginisortamab and 270 total gremlin-1 serum
concentrations (Wong 2026 Table S1 and Table S2).

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Wong_2026_ginisortamab")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every value below is the NONMEM final estimate in Wong 2026 Table 1. The
equations are those of the Supporting Information control stream (`$PK`,
`$DES`, `$ERROR`), which agree with the Figure 2 equations.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lcl` (CL) | log(0.433 L/day) | Table 1 |
| `lvc` (Vc at BSA 2 m^2) | log(4.38 L) | Table 1 |
| `lq` (Q) | log(0.849 L/day) | Table 1 |
| `lvp` (Vp at BSA 2 m^2) | log(3.23 L) | Table 1 |
| `e_bsa_vc` | 1.31 | Table 1; Figure 2 `(BSA/2)^1.3`; control stream `THETA(9)` |
| `e_bsa_vp` | 2.18 | Table 1; Figure 2 `(BSA/2)^2.2`; control stream `THETA(10)` |
| `lksyn` (Ksyn) | log(0.378 nmol/L/day) | Table 1 |
| `lkdeg` (Kdeg) | log(61.8 1/day) | Table 1 |
| `lkss` (Kss) | log(7.59 nmol/L) | Table 1 |
| `lkint` (Kint) | log(3.23 1/day) | Table 1 |
| `etalcl` | 0.051112 (22.9% CV) | Table 1; omega = log(1 + CV^2) per the Table 1 note |
| `etalvc`, `etalvp` block | 0.016504, 0.027092, 0.047265 (12.9% and 22.0% CV, r = 0.97) | Table 1; control stream `$OMEGA BLOCK(2)` |
| `etalkdeg` | 0.13555 (38.1% CV) | Table 1 |
| `etalkint` | 0.26767 (55.4% CV) | Table 1 |
| `propSd` | 0.108 | Table 1, RUV ginisortamab 10.8% |
| `propSd_Ctotal_target` | 0.356 | Table 1, RUV total gremlin-1 35.6% |
| `mw` = 150000 g/mol | - | control stream `$PK` (`MW = 150000`) |
| Free drug `cfree` (QSS root) | - | control stream `$DES` `CONC` |
| `d/dt(central)`, `d/dt(peripheral1)`, `d/dt(total_target)` | - | control stream `$DES` `DADT(1)`-`DADT(3)` |
| `total_target(0) = Ksyn/Kdeg` | - | control stream `$PK` (`A_0(3) = BLR`) |
| `Cc = cfree` (ug/mL), `Ctotal_target = total_target * MW/1000` (ng/mL) | - | control stream `$ERROR` (`IPRED`) |
| `tfree`, `target_suppression` | - | control stream `$ERROR` (`TFREE`); Methods, Modelling and simulation approaches |

# Typical-value checks

The paper reports a typical terminal half-life of about 13.3 days and a
gremlin-1 turnover time (1/Kdeg) of about 23 min (Results, Population PK/PD
model evaluation). Baseline total gremlin-1 is Ksyn/Kdeg, read on the ng/mL
scale with the control stream's conversion factor; Figure 1B shows pre-dose
total gremlin-1 near 1 ng/mL.

```{r typical-checks}
mod <- readModelDb("Wong_2026_ginisortamab")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta

cl <- exp(th[["lcl"]])
vc <- exp(th[["lvc"]])
q <- exp(th[["lq"]])
vp <- exp(th[["lvp"]])
kel <- cl / vc
k12 <- q / vc
k21 <- q / vp
beta <- 0.5 * (k12 + k21 + kel - sqrt((k12 + k21 + kel)^2 - 4 * k21 * kel))
thalf_beta <- log(2) / beta
turnover_min <- 1 / exp(th[["lkdeg"]]) * 24 * 60
baseline_ngml <- exp(th[["lksyn"]]) / exp(th[["lkdeg"]]) * 150000 / 1000

typical <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Terminal half-life (day)",
    "Gremlin-1 turnover time 1/Kdeg (min)",
    "Baseline total gremlin-1 (ng/mL)"
  ),
  Model = signif(c(thalf_beta, turnover_min, baseline_ngml), 3),
  Paper = c("~13.3", "~23", "~1 (Figure 1B, pre-dose)")
)
knitr::kable(typical, caption = "Closed-form typical values at BSA = 2 m^2.")

stopifnot(
  # Closed form from the published thetas; the paper's ~13.3 days is the
  # typical subject in its own covariate set, so allow a few percent.
  abs(thalf_beta / 13.3 - 1) < 0.05,
  abs(turnover_min / 23 - 1) < 0.05,
  baseline_ngml > 0.5, baseline_ngml < 2
)
```

# Virtual cohort

The published simulations used 1000 virtual subjects per regimen with BSA
resampled from the ONC001 participants. The individual BSA values are not
published, so BSA is drawn here from a log-normal distribution with median
1.8 m^2 truncated to the observed range 1.4-2.4 m^2 (Table S1). Each regimen
has 200 subjects.

Nine regimens are simulated, as in Table 2 and Table S3: the five
dose-escalation regimens (100-2000 mg Q2W, 60-min infusion, six 28-day
cycles), the hypothetical 1000 mg once-weekly (QW) regimen (60-min infusion,
six 28-day cycles), and the three dose-optimisation regimens (2000 mg Q2W
30-min infusion, six 28-day cycles; 3000 mg Q3W 90-min infusion, eight 21-day
cycles; 4000 mg Q4W 120-min infusion, six 28-day cycles).

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20260430)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20260430)

regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,               ~dose, ~tau, ~n_dose, ~inf_min,
  "100 mg Q2W, 60 min",     100,   14,      12,       60,
  "250 mg Q2W, 60 min",     250,   14,      12,       60,
  "500 mg Q2W, 60 min",     500,   14,      12,       60,
  "1000 mg Q2W, 60 min",   1000,   14,      12,       60,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 60 min",   2000,   14,      12,       60,
  "1000 mg QW, 60 min",    1000,    7,      24,       60,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 30 min",   2000,   14,      12,       30,
  "3000 mg Q3W, 90 min",   3000,   21,       8,       90,
  "4000 mg Q4W, 120 min",  4000,   28,       6,      120
) |>
  mutate(
    dur = inf_min / 60 / 24,
    t_last = (n_dose - 1) * tau
  )

n_per_regimen <- 200L

sample_bsa <- function(n) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    x <- rlnorm(2 * n, meanlog = log(1.8), sdlog = 0.12)
    out <- c(out, x[x >= 1.4 & x <= 2.4])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

make_regimen <- function(i, n, id_offset) {
  r <- regimens[i, ]
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose_times <- (seq_len(r$n_dose) - 1) * r$tau
  obs_times <- sort(unique(round(c(
    seq(0, r$t_last + 70, by = 0.5),
    seq(0, r$tau, by = 0.1),
    seq(r$t_last, r$t_last + r$tau, by = 0.1),
    r$dur,
    r$t_last + r$dur
  ), 6)))
  subj <- tibble(id = ids, BSA = sample_bsa(n), regimen = r$regimen)
  doses <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = dose_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 1L, amt = r$dose, dur = r$dur, cmt = "central", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::crossing(subj, time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, dur = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs)
}

events <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  make_regimen(i, n_per_regimen, id_offset = (i - 1L) * n_per_regimen)
})) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid)) |>
  as.data.frame()

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")]))
```

# Simulation

The model has two endpoints (free ginisortamab `Cc` and total gremlin-1
`Ctotal_target`), so observation rows carry `dvid = 1` on the `central` state;
rxode2 returns every output column on every observation row.

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(
  mod,
  events = events,
  keep = c("regimen", "BSA"),
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  left_join(regimens |> select(regimen, tau, t_last, dur), by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen))
```

# Replicate published figures

```{r figure-1, fig.height = 7}
# Replicates Figure 1 of Wong 2026: free ginisortamab (A) and total gremlin-1
# (B) by dose for the dose-escalation regimens (simulated median and 5th-95th
# percentiles; the figure shows observed data and their medians).
esc <- sim |>
  filter(grepl("Q2W, 60 min", regimen)) |>
  mutate(dose = factor(sub(" Q2W.*", "", regimen), levels = paste(c(100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000), "mg")))

pa <- esc |>
  filter(time >= 1 / 24, time <= 98) |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), Q50 = median(Cc), Q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = dose, fill = dose)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_y_log10() +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (days)", y = "Free ginisortamab (ug/mL)",
       colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
       title = "Figure 1A - ginisortamab serum concentration")

pb <- esc |>
  filter(time <= 14) |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(Ctotal_target, 0.05), Q50 = median(Ctotal_target),
    Q95 = quantile(Ctotal_target, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50, colour = dose, fill = dose)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (days)", y = "Total gremlin-1 (ng/mL)",
       colour = "Dose", fill = "Dose",
       title = "Figure 1B - total gremlin-1 serum concentration",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 1 of Wong 2026 (simulated median and 90% interval).")

print(pa)
print(pb)
```

The simulated median total gremlin-1 rises within a day from about 1 ng/mL
to about 8 ng/mL at 100 mg and about 17 ng/mL at 2000 mg, and stays higher at
the higher doses through the dosing interval, as in Figure 1B: once gremlin-1
is bound, its loss is governed by Kint (3.23/day) rather than by the much
faster Kdeg (61.8/day).

```{r figure-5, fig.height = 6}
# Replicates Figure 5 of Wong 2026: predicted percent gremlin-1 suppression
# over six 28-day cycles of the dose-escalation regimens.
esc |>
  filter(time <= 168) |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(target_suppression, 0.05),
    Q50 = median(target_suppression),
    Q95 = quantile(target_suppression, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(time, Q50)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~dose, ncol = 2) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time (days)", y = "Target suppression (%)",
       title = "Figure 5 - gremlin-1 suppression, dose-escalation regimens",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 5 of Wong 2026 (median and 90% prediction interval).")
```

```{r figure-6}
# Replicates Figure 6 of Wong 2026: median suppression from the start of the
# last 28-day cycle (doses at 140 and 154 days) through washout.
esc |>
  filter(time >= 140, time <= 140 + 84) |>
  group_by(dose, time) |>
  summarise(Q50 = median(target_suppression), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time - 140, Q50, colour = dose)) +
  geom_line() +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 84, by = 14)) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 100)) +
  labs(x = "Time since start of last cycle (days)", y = "Target suppression (%)",
       colour = "Dose",
       title = "Figure 6 - median suppression after repeated dosing",
       caption = "Replicates Figure 6 of Wong 2026.")
```

# Target suppression against Table 2

Table 2 reports the median (90% prediction interval) suppression at the end
of the dosing interval and the maximum suppression within the interval, after
the first dose and after the last dose (steady state).

```{r table-2}
supp <- bind_rows(
  sim |>
    filter(time >= 0, time <= tau) |>
    mutate(period = "First dose"),
  sim |>
    filter(time >= t_last, time <= t_last + tau) |>
    mutate(period = "Last dose")
) |>
  group_by(regimen, period, id) |>
  summarise(
    end = target_suppression[which.max(time)],
    max = max(target_suppression),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

supp_sim <- supp |>
  group_by(regimen, period) |>
  summarise(
    end_med = median(end), end_lo = quantile(end, 0.05), end_hi = quantile(end, 0.95),
    max_med = median(max), max_lo = quantile(max, 0.05), max_hi = quantile(max, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

supp_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,               ~period,      ~end_pub, ~max_pub,
  "100 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",       18,       87,
  "250 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",       35,       94,
  "500 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",       53,       97,
  "1000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "First dose",       69,       98,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "First dose",       82,       99,
  "1000 mg QW, 60 min",   "First dose",       77,       98,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 30 min",  "First dose",       82,       99,
  "3000 mg Q3W, 90 min",  "First dose",       81,       99,
  "4000 mg Q4W, 120 min", "First dose",       80,       99,
  "100 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",        29,       77,
  "250 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",        51,       86,
  "500 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",        68,       91,
  "1000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "Last dose",        81,       95,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "Last dose",        89,       97,
  "1000 mg QW, 60 min",   "Last dose",        91,       96,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 30 min",  "Last dose",        89,       97,
  "3000 mg Q3W, 90 min",  "Last dose",        86,       98,
  "4000 mg Q4W, 120 min", "Last dose",        83,       98
)

supp_cmp <- supp_pub |>
  mutate(regimen = factor(regimen, levels = regimens$regimen)) |>
  left_join(supp_sim, by = c("regimen", "period")) |>
  mutate(d_end = end_med - end_pub, d_max = max_med - max_pub) |>
  arrange(period, regimen)

supp_cmp |>
  transmute(
    regimen, period,
    end_sim = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", end_med, end_lo, end_hi),
    end_pub, d_end = round(d_end, 1),
    max_sim = sprintf("%.0f (%.0f-%.0f)", max_med, max_lo, max_hi),
    max_pub, d_max = round(d_max, 1)
  ) |>
  rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen,
    "Period" = period,
    "End of interval, simulated (%)" = end_sim,
    "End of interval, Table 2 (%)" = end_pub,
    "Difference (points)" = d_end,
    "Maximum, simulated (%)" = max_sim,
    "Maximum, Table 2 (%)" = max_pub,
    "Difference, max (points)" = d_max
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median (5th-95th percentile) simulated suppression against the Table 2 medians.")

stopifnot(
  # A mis-transcribed Kdeg, Kss, Kint or Ksyn moves these medians by tens of
  # percentage points; the remaining gap is Monte Carlo error and the
  # unpublished BSA sample.
  abs(median(supp_cmp$d_end)) < 4,
  max(abs(supp_cmp$d_end)) < 12,
  max(abs(supp_cmp$d_max)) < 6
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Free ginisortamab exposure after the first dose and after the last dose is
computed with PKNCA over each dosing interval and compared with the medians of
Table S3. `cav` is AUCtau divided by tau, as defined in the paper.

```{r pknca}
nca_window <- bind_rows(
  sim |> filter(time >= 0, time <= tau),
  sim |> filter(time >= t_last, time <= t_last + tau)
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, regimen) |>
  mutate(regimen = as.character(regimen)) |>
  distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  arrange(id, time)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_window, Cc ~ time | regimen + id)

dose_df <- events |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, regimen)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | regimen + id)

# Table S3 Cmin is the end-of-interval trough. Over the first interval the
# PKNCA minimum is the pre-dose zero, so the trough is read with `ctrough`
# there; over the last interval the minimum is the trough, read with `cmin`.
intervals <- bind_rows(
  regimens |> transmute(regimen, start = 0, end = tau, ctrough = TRUE, cmin = FALSE),
  regimens |> transmute(regimen, start = t_last, end = t_last + tau, ctrough = FALSE, cmin = TRUE)
) |>
  mutate(cmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE)

nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_long <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  left_join(regimens |> select(regimen, t_last), by = "regimen") |>
  mutate(
    period = ifelse(start == 0, "First dose", "Last dose"),
    PPTESTCD = ifelse(PPTESTCD == "ctrough", "cmin", PPTESTCD)
  ) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast", "cav")) |>
  select(regimen, period, PPTESTCD, PPORRES)
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~regimen,               ~period,       ~cmin,  ~cav,   ~cmax,   ~auclast,
  "100 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",   5.05,  10.2,    28.7,    143.4,
  "250 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",   12.7,  25.7,    71.9,    359.2,
  "500 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "First dose",   25.5,  51.4,   143.7,    719.4,
  "1000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "First dose",   51.1, 102.8,   287.4,   1439.8,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "First dose",  102.5, 205.8,   574.9,   2881.3,
  "1000 mg QW, 60 min",   "First dose",  82.27, 140.5,   288.9,    983.6,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 30 min",  "First dose",  102.7, 208.0,   583.5,   2912.0,
  "3000 mg Q3W, 90 min",  "First dose",  105.5, 250.3,   855.2,   5256.3,
  "4000 mg Q4W, 120 min", "First dose",   91.9, 278.0,  1117.9,   7784.8,
  "100 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",     9.4,  16.8,    40.2,    235.1,
  "250 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",    23.7,  42.2,   100.8,    590.8,
  "500 mg Q2W, 60 min",   "Last dose",    47.5,  84.7,   201.9,   1185.5,
  "1000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "Last dose",    95.4, 169.9,   404.1,   2378.1,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 60 min",  "Last dose",   191.2, 340.3,   808.7,   4764.0,
  "1000 mg QW, 60 min",   "Last dose",   245.1, 343.5,   578.9,   2404.7,
  "2000 mg Q2W, 30 min",  "Last dose",   192.4, 341.1,   822.8,   4774.8,
  "3000 mg Q3W, 90 min",  "Last dose",   153.5, 346.8,  1039.9,   7282.6,
  "4000 mg Q4W, 120 min", "Last dose",   115.5, 341.2,  1267.9,   9552.7
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_long,
  reference = published,
  by = c("regimen", "period"),
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cmin = "ug/mL", cav = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*day/mL"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste(
    "Simulated (median of 200 subjects) vs. Table S3 medians.",
    "AUC is AUCtau over the dosing interval.",
    if (!is.null(attr(cmp, "footnote"))) attr(cmp, "footnote") else ""
  )
)

pct <- nca_long |>
  group_by(regimen, period, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(sim = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  inner_join(
    published |> pivot_longer(c(cmin, cav, cmax, auclast), names_to = "PPTESTCD", values_to = "ref"),
    by = c("regimen", "period", "PPTESTCD")
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (sim / ref - 1))

stopifnot(
  # One row per regimen, period and parameter.
  nrow(pct) == 72,
  # AUC and Cav are governed by CL alone (no covariate on CL), so a
  # mis-transcribed clearance or dose shifts them all together by tens of
  # percent. The simulated medians sit about 4% below Table S3 (see text).
  abs(median(pct$pct_diff[pct$PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cav")])) < 10,
  quantile(abs(pct$pct_diff), 0.9) < 20
)
```

The AUC and Cav medians agree with Table S3 within about 7% across all nine
regimens (typically about 4% low), and Cmin within about 6% after both the
first and the last dose.
Cmax runs about 8-14% below the Table S3 medians. Cmax depends on Vc and
therefore on the BSA distribution, which the paper resampled from the
individual ONC001 values that are not published; the virtual cohort here is
centred at the Table S1 median of 1.8 m^2. A smaller BSA in the paper's
resampled cohort would raise Cmax and, slightly, AUCtau, which fits the
direction of both gaps. The parameters were not adjusted.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Units and molecular weight.** The authors' control stream works in nmol and
  nmol/L and converts both analytes to ng/mL with a molecular weight of
  150000 g/mol (`IPRED = CONC1*(MW/1000)` for ginisortamab and
  `IPRED = A(3)*(MW/1000)` for total gremlin-1). The packaged model takes doses
  in mg, converts the central amount to nmol/L with the same 150 kDa factor,
  returns free ginisortamab in ug/mL and total gremlin-1 in ng/mL with the
  control stream's factor. Gremlin-1 is a far smaller protein than an IgG, so
  Ksyn, Kss and the baseline are nominal nmol/L on that 150 kDa scale; they
  reproduce the fitted ng/mL data (pre-dose total gremlin-1 about 1 ng/mL in
  Figure 1B) and must be read back with the same factor.
- **BSA centring.** The control stream and Figure 2 centre BSA at 2 m^2, and the
  Results call 2 m^2 the participant median, but Table S1 reports a median of
  1.8 m^2 (range 1.4-2.4). The fitted centring constant 2 m^2 is used.
- **Virtual BSA distribution.** The paper resampled individual BSA values that
  are not published; a log-normal (median 1.8 m^2, log-SD 0.12) truncated to
  1.4-2.4 m^2 is used instead. Cmax is the metric most sensitive to this
  choice.
- **Cohort size.** 200 virtual subjects per regimen rather than the paper's
  1000.
- **Free drug.** The bridging assay measures free ginisortamab (Methods,
  Sampling and bioanalytical methods), so `Cc` is the free concentration from
  the QSS root, as in the control stream.
- **Target suppression.** `target_suppression` is
  `100 * (1 - tfree / (Ksyn/Kdeg))`, the percent change in free gremlin-1
  relative to the individual model baseline (Methods, Modelling and simulation
  approaches); free gremlin-1 is the control stream's `TFREE`.
- No erratum or correction notice was found for this article (Europe PMC
  search, 2026-11-15).
